lineage: Encryptor is a modified build of the leaked Babuk source code; 2026 pre-ransomware tradecraft linked to Velvet Tempest (DEV-0504), a long-time Ryuk/REvil/Conti affiliate
summary: Termite is a double-extortion operation that surfaced in late 2024 with high-profile victims including supply-chain SaaS provider Blue Yonder and Australian IVF provider Genea. Symantec assessed its encryptor as a modified Babuk build appending .termite. Early intrusions were circumstantially linked to mass exploitation of Cleo managed-file-transfer flaws (attribution unconfirmed); in 2026 MalBeacon observed the Termite-linked affiliate Velvet Tempest using ClickFix malvertising, finger.exe/PowerShell loaders, csc.exe-compiled .NET components, DonutLoader and CastleRAT ahead of ransomware.
uniqueTraits: Supply-chain impact: targets SaaS/logistics providers (Blue Yonder) for cascading downstream disruption
Possible exploitation of Cleo MFT flaws (CVE-2024-50623 / CVE-2024-55956) for initial access — reported, not confirmed
Velvet Tempest pre-ransomware chain: ClickFix fake CAPTCHA -> Run-dialog paste -> finger.exe fetch -> csc.exe compile -> DonutLoader -> CastleRAT
Chrome credential harvesting via PowerShell script hosted on Termite tool-staging infrastructure
Babuk-derived locker: API-based service/process stops, shadow-copy deletion, Recycle Bin clearing, network-share encryption

sources.title: Cleo File Transfer Vulnerability Under Exploitation (Symantec comment on Termite = modified Babuk)

chain.procedure: Reported exploitation of Cleo Harmony/VLTrader/LexiCom file-transfer flaws (CVE-2024-50623, CVE-2024-55956) around the Blue Yonder intrusion; researchers note Cl0p claimed the campaign and Termite involvement is unconfirmed.
chain.noAtomicReason: No local Atomic Red Team test exploits Cleo MFT (or any T1190 web-application exploit); validate with perimeter/WAF and file-transfer server telemetry instead.
